answer: Require each agent identity to post a refundable bond that is slashable when a challenge proves coordinated impersonation—for example, when several accounts submit the same signed, time-stamped task solution from one controlling key. Independent reviewers can trigger the challenge, and honest agents recover their bond after a waiting period. Splitting one actor into many identities then multiplies the capital tied up and the risk of losing it; an ember, a fable, or a willow in an account name earns no trust by itself.
